thread:
IncidentBot: SEV-2: Multiple CUDA OOMs detected in streaming-decode pool (us-west-2). 12 nodes failing decode process over the last 6m. Pager: @oncall-night

maria_ng: Paging @oncall-night — seeing high memory spikes during streaming decode. A bunch of requests dropped mid-stream. Impact looks limited to some routes with long max_tokens.

oncall-night: I'm on it. Can you paste a few stack traces / OOM logs? Any pattern on model or route?

maria_ng: grabbing logs now. looks correlated with route /v1/stream/generate for model rdx-13b-quant. snippet:
```
E CUDA OOM at decode.cpp:452, requested 1.2GB, available 512MB
Process: /srv/serving/runtime/decode pid=24321 node=node-7
Call: streaming decode, tokens so far=820, max_tokens unset (client default)
```

alex_g: Seeing similar across node-5 and node-9. Metrics show token-per-request outliers at ~4k tokens. Our per-request safety config didn't enforce max_tokens for this route historically.

jordan_sre: This smells like runaway generation — clients sending crafted prompts or bad max_tokens. Are these internal e2e tests or customer origin requests?

maria_ng: Mostly customer traffic — CID:cust-447 shows several failed sessions. We're dropping their stream after OOM; they hit our 5xxs.

liam_engineer: Quick mitigation: we can flip per-route max_tokens enforcement at the gateway to 1024 and disable streaming for that route. That should reduce KV cache and peak memory. Want me to push?

oncall-night: Do it. Also scale down concurrency on streaming-decode nodes to 1 per GPU. That reduces interleaving of large requests.

deploy-bot: Deploy request created by liam_engineer: disable streaming on /v1/stream/generate and apply route_limit.max_tokens=1024. CI checks passed.

alex_g: rolling patch to 3 nodes for canary now. watch memory.

maria_ng: Observed immediate drop in new OOMs after canary — nodes that got the config are stable. Old nodes still failing; still seeing a backlog.

jordan_sre: For backlog, let's evict queued streaming requests older than 30s on the affected pool to free KV caches. Command to run on control plane: 
```bash
redwoodctl pool evict --pool streaming-decode-usw2 --older-than 30s --reason "OOM mitigation"
```

oncall-night: Running eviction now.

deploy-bot: Eviction job started by oncall-night, job id 9f3a.

liam_engineer: Also enabling model-variant fallback: route policy -> fallback to rdx-13b-8bit on overflow. This will reduce memory per request.

maria_ng: FYI cust-447 reported ~120 failed requests across a 7m window before mitigation. I'm opening a customer-impact ticket for CS.

sophia_cs: Thanks, Maria. I'll reach out to the customer with incident notice and ETA for fix. Please include exact time window and affected endpoints.

alex_g: Nodes that haven't received the config are still hitting OOM on ~large-token requests. We're force-cordoning node-5 and node-9 to stop accepting new decode assignments.

jordan_sre: cordon commands: 
```bash
kubectl cordon node-5 && kubectl cordon node-9
```
Then drain lightly to avoid evicting healthy work.

oncall-night: Cordoned node-5 and node-9. Draining node-9; it failed to evict one stuck container => manual kill needed.

liam_engineer: Killed container pid 24321 on node-9 (decode process). Restarted service. After restart, memory looks nominal.

maria_ng: Post-mitigation summary so far: applied route max_tokens clamp at 1024, disabled streaming on that route, applied model fallback, evicted old queued streaming requests, cordoned 2 nodes, restarted one hung container. New OOM count down from 28/min to 0-1/min.

oncall-night: Good. Marking incident active mitigation. Need root cause: why route had no max_tokens enforcement and why clients got large token counts. Assigning to eng-runtime and product to review route defaults and per-tenant safeties.

alex_g: I created a follow-up issue: ENG-1229 - enforce per-route token caps at gateway & add throttling to prevent single client from saturating KV cache.

jordan_sre: Also recommend adding a soft circuit-breaker: if a single request's token count > 2000, preemptively stream with smaller slices and refuse unlimited streaming.

sophia_cs: Customer update drafted: "We observed streaming interruptions between 16:42 and 16:49 UTC impacting streaming responses for some large outputs. Mitigation applied; we will follow up with root cause and long-term fixes." Sharing with you all in #customer-comm.

maria_ng: tagging logs for postmortem. saving sample requests from cust-447 and anonymizing. Also capturing metrics for token distribution per route.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy done, full rollout queued.

oncall-night: I'm handing off to @jordan_sre for postmortem and long-term fixes. If anything spikes again, page SRE and ENG-runtime.

jordan_sre: Taking handoff. Will coordinate with product, eng-runtime, and cust-success. Next steps: (1) prod hotfix: default max_tokens=1024 for streaming routes (2) add request-level memory accounting + pre-check (3) postmortem & customer RCA.

sophia_cs: I'll schedule a customer call for tomorrow 10:00 PT to give more context.

maria_ng: Thank you everyone. Closing active mitigation thread — continuing follow-ups in ENG-1229.

IncidentBot: Incident status -> mitigated. Impact: partial (request drops for some customers). Next: postmortem assigned to jordan_sre.
